messages.content: Milwaukee changed a little. The museum timed entry is now late Saturday morning, 11:15, and my sister can only do Bay View brunch Sunday at 10:30. We still get in close to 8 Friday. Can you compare the lakefront hold against the Homewood hold before I let one go?
Yes. I’ll compare them around the new timing, not just the nightly rate. Are you still trying to keep Friday dinner simple and avoid extra rideshares where possible?
Exactly. If we need one rideshare to Bay View, fine, but I don’t want the hotel choice creating more.

Quick view:
| Hotel | Est. total | Friday arrival/dinner | Sat museum | Sun Bay View brunch | Room/breakfast | Trade-off |
| Lakefront hold | about $498 | easiest on-site dinner, but a longer hop from the train | 5-8 min walk | 12-15 min rideshare | coffee + mini-fridge listed; breakfast not included | simplest Friday night, higher cost |
| Homewood Downtown/Third Ward | $454.20 held | closer to Intermodal; restaurants 5-8 min walk, check late hours | 15-18 min walk or short streetcar/rideshare | 10-12 min rideshare | king studio, coffee, fridge/kitchenette, included breakfast | saves about $44; no true on-site dinner |
Is Homewood actually less hassle from the station?

Yes. From Intermodal, Homewood is the easier arrival: roughly a 6-minute rideshare or a manageable walk if you are not tired. The lakefront place is prettier for Saturday, but it does not improve Sunday.
And dinner after 8?
Lakefront wins if you want to walk downstairs. Homewood still works if you are comfortable with a short Third Ward walk; I would pick a place with later hours before you board the train.
Then keep Homewood. Please cancel the lakefront backup before its deadline and keep the quiet one-bed request.

Done. Homewood Suites Milwaukee Downtown remains the active hold for June 25-27: one non-smoking king studio suite, quiet room requested, estimated $454.20, refundable through June 23 at 11:59 p.m. I cancelled the lakefront backup and left train, museum entry, and Bay View brunch unchanged.

messages.content: Starting Denver: August 24-26 for the regional arts data convening. Tuesday evening opening reception downtown, Wednesday full day near the convention center, Thursday grantmaker roundtable expected to end at noon. I’m flying from Chicago, no rental car. Can you compare flight and hotel pairings with totals? I’d like to return Thursday after lunch but not turn it into a late evening.
Sure. Before I pair them: is ORD preferred over Midway, any airline preference, carry-on only, and do you have a lodging cap before tax?

ORD is easier, MDW is okay if the savings are real. United is fine if it lines up. Carry-on only. Lodging should stay around $250 before tax, and please include breakfast and room basics for the non-block hotels.

Using two hotel nights and a carry-on, here is the compact scan. Est. total = airfare + hotel with tax + about $34 for A Line/local transfers; meals not included.
| Pairing | Flights | Hotel / meeting access | Breakfast + room basics | Dinner/cancel | Est. total |
| A. United + Hyatt convention block | ORD-DEN Tue 10:05-11:50; Thu 2:25-5:55 | Hyatt Regency at convention center, 2-3 min walk | no included breakfast; coffee in room; mini-fridge listed but I would confirm at booking | on-site restaurant; block closes Aug. 6; cancel by Aug. 20 | about $860 |
| B. United + Hampton Convention Center | same United flights | 5-6 min walk to sessions | included hot breakfast; standard king listed; coffee + mini-fridge | no full dinner restaurant, but several within 3-6 min; cancel by Aug. 21 | about $766 |
| C. Southwest + Home2 Convention Center | MDW-DEN Tue 9:20-10:55; Thu 1:55-5:20 | 7-8 min walk | included breakfast; studio with coffee + full fridge/kitchenette | limited-service; dinner off-site; cancel by Aug. 21 | about $713 |
| D. American + The Slate | ORD-DEN Tue 12:15-2:00; Thu 3:10-6:39 | 6 min walk | no included breakfast; coffee + mini-fridge listed | good on-site restaurant; cancel by Aug. 21 | about $827 |
Which one has the least friction without overpaying?

The Hampton plus United pairing is the clean middle. It keeps ORD, a good arrival cushion before the Tuesday reception, breakfast included, and only a short walk to the convention center. The Hyatt block is easiest once you are downtown, but the extra roughly $95 mostly buys the very short walk and on-site dinner. Home2 saves the most, but it is a little more limited-service and uses Midway.
Can you check whether Hampton and Home2 really have a one-bed room, coffee, and a fridge? I don’t want a surprise there.

Listed availability right now: Hampton has a standard king non-smoking room with in-room coffee and mini-fridge, plus included breakfast. Home2 has a king studio suite with coffee and a full-size refrigerator/kitchenette, also with breakfast. I would still verify those on the booking screen before payment because downtown Denver inventory can change.
Is the airport train reasonable with a bag?

Yes for Tuesday. The A Line from DEN to Union Station is about 37 minutes, then a free downtown connector/light rail segment or short rideshare to the convention center hotels. With just a carry-on, no rental car is needed. For Thursday, the train is fine only if the meeting ends on time and you are not cutting the flight close.
Is that 2:25 United return too tight if the roundtable ends right at noon?

It is workable but not relaxed. You would need bags stored at the hotel, leave downtown around 12:15-12:20, and likely use a direct rideshare to DEN. If you want to use the train or have any chance of a late finish, a departure closer to 3:00 is safer.
Can you rerun the return with something later but still not late evening? United if comparable.

Later-return version: United DEN-ORD 3:35-7:07 is about $312 round trip; American 3:10-6:39 is about $304; Southwest to MDW 3:00-6:25 is about $278. With Hampton, that makes the totals about $792 on United, $784 on American, or $758 on Southwest. The American return is the best timing/value balance; United is close if ORD and carrier consistency matter more than about $8.
Would the block hotel make the 2:25 United return safe enough to justify the extra cost?

Not by itself. The block hotel saves maybe 5-8 downtown minutes; the airport transfer is the real constraint. If you choose 2:25, I would plan on a rideshare regardless of hotel. If you choose a 3-ish return, Hampton becomes much easier to defend because you save money and still have a short meeting walk.
Let’s not ticket yet. Save a ranked shortlist and the hotel cancellation dates, please.

Saved, no bookings made. Ranked shortlist: 1) Hampton Convention Center with a 3-ish ORD return, best balance of cost, breakfast, and access; cancel by Aug. 21. 2) Hyatt block if the agenda shifts into the hotel or you want on-site dinner; block closes Aug. 6 and cancels by Aug. 20. 3) Home2 if the savings matter more than service level and Midway is acceptable; cancel by Aug. 21. I also noted that a 2:25 return needs a direct rideshare and an on-time noon finish.

messages.content: Denver update: Wednesday’s networking reception is in RiNo, and the Thursday roundtable may now run until 12:45. The hotel block closes in three days. Can we narrow the hotel choice between the Hyatt block and the breakfast hotels? Please check total cost, walk time, coffee/fridge, one-bed room, dinner access, and what this does to the return flight.
Yes. The later Thursday finish matters more for the flight than the hotel, but I’ll compare both. Are you assuming you will store your bag at the hotel Thursday morning?
Yes, bag at the hotel. No rental car. I’d rather keep mornings easy, but the lodging total has to be defensible.

Updated hotel view, two nights with taxes:
| Hotel | Est. total | Meeting/RiNo access | Breakfast + room basics | Dinner/cancel | Return-flight impact |
| Hyatt block | $544 | 2-3 min to convention center; 10-15 min rideshare to RiNo | no included breakfast; standard king in block; coffee; mini-fridge listed/confirm | on-site restaurant; block closes Aug. 6; cancel by Aug. 20 | saves only a few minutes Thursday; still not enough for a 2:25 flight after a 12:45 finish |
| Hampton Convention Center | $448 | 5-6 min walk; 10-15 min rideshare to RiNo | included breakfast; standard king available; coffee + mini-fridge | nearby restaurants, no full on-site dinner; cancel by Aug. 21 | works well with 3:10+ return; breakfast helps the total |
| Home2 Convention Center | $421 | 7-8 min walk; 10-15 min rideshare to RiNo | included breakfast; king studio with coffee + full fridge/kitchenette | limited-service; nearby dinner; cancel by Aug. 21 | cheapest, but adds a bit more walking/service friction |
Is the Hampton king actually available, not just a general room type?

Yes, the current refundable listing shows a standard king non-smoking room. It lists in-room coffee, mini-fridge, Wi-Fi, and included breakfast. I would select the king room explicitly rather than leaving bedding assigned at check-in.
Home2 saves a little more. Is it worth dropping to that?

For about $27 less than Hampton, I do not think so. Home2 has the best kitchenette setup, but Hampton gives you a slightly shorter walk, a more conventional hotel setup, and the same breakfast value. The bigger savings are versus the Hyatt, not between Hampton and Home2.
Would the Hyatt help enough on Thursday if the roundtable goes to 12:45?

Only marginally. It might get you to your bag and curb 5 minutes faster. A 2:25 departure is still too tight. I would target American around 3:10 or United around 3:35; if you choose the earlier of those, use a rideshare to DEN.
So Hampton is defensible even with a block hotel available?

Yes. It saves roughly $96 versus the block, includes breakfast for both mornings, keeps the Wednesday walk under 10 minutes, and has the room basics confirmed. The RiNo reception requires a short rideshare from any of these, so the block does not solve that piece.
Please hold Hampton refundable, standard one-bed, quiet if available. Don’t ticket flights yet; note the 3-ish return.

Held: Hampton Inn & Suites Denver Downtown-Convention Center, August 24-26, refundable standard king non-smoking room, estimated total $447.60 with taxes. Added a quiet-room request and noted included breakfast, in-room coffee, and mini-fridge. Cancellation deadline saved as August 21 at 11:59 p.m. Flights are not ticketed; I noted no return earlier than about 3:10 if Thursday runs to 12:45, with the United 3:35 return as the cleaner ORD option.
